title: HEAD_DIM 64 + 2^18 batch at device batch 128
description: HEAD_DIM 128->64 (8 heads of 64 at unchanged dim 512, so params/FLOPs are identical), TOTAL_BATCH_SIZE 2^17->2^18, DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 64->128 (grad_accum stays 1).
reflection: val_bpb 0.994131, MFU 37.60%, 469.5M tokens, 1791 steps, peak VRAM 45.0GB. Restoring device batch 128 did what round 0's data predicted for throughput: MFU 33.5% -> 37.6%, tokens 420M -> 469.5M (+12%). But that is ALSO the whole story: round 0's five byte-identical replicas gave slope -0.000097 bpb per 1M tokens, which extrapolates 422M/0.996458 to ~0.9919 at 469.5M. I measured 0.994131, i.e. slightly WORSE than the pure-token extrapolation. So neither halving head_dim nor doubling the optimizer batch bought anything beyond the extra tokens, and the honest effect size of my two architectural/optimizer changes is zero or mildly negative. The transferable conclusion is that throughput is the only axis that has moved anything in nine runs, and it is nearly exhausted: 37.6% MFU on a 50M-param model at device batch 128 is close to what this shape gives. Everything else we have tried (batch count 4x, head count 2x) has landed inside the 0.00187 replication sd. Future rounds should either target token-efficiency changes large enough to clear ~0.004 in one run, or accept that ranking requires replication.
